CardFile.description: One file under cards/: the definition, its status, where it came from, and the scenarios that verify it. Written only by the pipeline.

CardDefinition.description: One card as the engine sees it: its faces and what they do. Nothing about price, art or set; those live in the Scryfall object the card came from.

Provenance.description: How the definition in a card file came to be.

Scenario.description: A test as data: a board, a sequence of actions, and what must be true afterwards. A ruling, a rulebook example, a bug report and a hand-written check all take this shape, and the engine runs them all through the same runner.

TranslationCandidate.description: One model's reading, kept when the readings disagreed so the dispute view can show both.

Verification.description: The runner's record of the last verification: which engine, which run, how many scenarios passed.

Face.description: One face of a card: the printed characteristics, CR 109.3, and its abilities. Power and toughness stay as printed so "*" survives; the engine reads the number when there is one.

ExcludedProvenance.description: On the published exclusion list, with the reason.

HumanProvenance.description: Corrected by a person through the pipeline's edit command.

TemplateProvenance.description: Written straight from the Scryfall JSON: keyword-only, vanilla, or a mana pattern.

TranslatedProvenance.description: Written by the translation stage. Agreed is whether both models produced the same definition.

autoAnswer.description: Who answers the questions the game stops to ask (CR 101.4). A scenario generated from the definition — the smoke scenario — sets this true: it has never seen the game's objects, so it cannot name an option id, and the runner answers every question with the first legal option, recorded as a real AnswerChoice command so the log still replays. A hand-written scenario leaves it false and answers itself with AnswerStep: the answer it picks is usually the point of the test, and a runner that answered first-legal would erase it.

ScenarioSetup.description: The board before the first step. Cards are named; the runner resolves names through the definition store.

ScenarioStep.description: One thing a player does, or the runner does for them.

Expectation.description: What must hold after the steps.

TypeLine.description: The type line, CR 205: supertypes, types, subtypes.

PrintedStat.description: Printed power or toughness: a number, or a characteristic-defining marker such as "*".

Ability.description: The six shapes an ability can take, CR 113.3, plus the keyword form. Every line of a card's text is one of these.

Cost.description: What a player pays, CR 118. Mana is written as printed ("{1}{G}", "{X}{X}"); everything else is a record. A cost that asks for a choice takes it with the activation, so the engine never suspends a payment.

Condition.description: A yes-or-no question about the game: an intervening "if" on a trigger, the "as long as" of a static ability, the "if" of an effect. Ability words are conditions here, not nodes of their own.

ClassLevel.description: A Class card's level, CR 716: the cost to reach it and what it adds.

GeneratedSource.description: Generated by the pipeline from the definition itself: the smoke scenario.

ReportSource.description: A player's report from a game log position.

RulebookExampleSource.description: An "Example:" paragraph from the Comprehensive Rules, by rule number.

RulingSource.description: A Scryfall ruling, quoted, on the card the scenario belongs to.

costObjects.description: The objects the activation cost eats, chosen at CR 602.2b and paid at CR 601.2h — the same field, and the same reason, as CastStep.CostObjects.

ActivateStep.description: A player activates an ability (CR 602.2), by its index in the face's ability list.

AnswerStep.description: Answer the pending question: a choice's option ids, in order.

costObjects.description: The objects a printed cost eats, chosen as the spell is cast (CR 601.2c) and paid for at CR 601.2h: the creature a "Sacrifice a creature" cost sacrifices, the cards an exile cost exiles. Without them the engine has to guess, and refuses instead — "There are not enough permanents to sacrifice" is the refusal a scenario gets for leaving this null.

CastStep.description: A player casts a card (CR 601.2). Cards, targets and cost objects are named by the alias the setup gave them, or by card name where no name repeats.

ExpectRefusedStep.description: The next step must be refused by the engine, with a reason containing the text.

ResolveAllStep.description: Every player passes until the stack is empty.

AttachedToIs.description: One permanent is attached to another (CR 301.5, 303.4f): the Aura, Equipment or Fortification named by Card is attached to the object named by To. This is what an Aura scenario means; asserting the Aura is merely on the battlefield passes for a moment and then stops, because CR 704.5m puts an unattached Aura into its owner's graveyard. Named for TappedIs and not AttachedTo, which is the predicate a card's own filter uses ("Auras attached to it"); one discriminator, one meaning.

EventLogged.description: An event of the given kind was logged, optionally mentioning a card.

ManaPoolIs.description: A player's mana pool holds exactly this mana (CR 106.4). Written the way a mana cost is — "{G}{G}", "{2}{U}" — and read as a total, not an order: a pool is a bag of symbols, so the expectation compares what is in it and not how it got there. The empty string is an empty pool. This is what a "add {G} to your mana pool" card should assert; the event it logged says only that mana changed, which is true of a card that added the wrong colour.

ActivatedAbility.description: "[Cost]: [Effect]", CR 602. Loyalty abilities carry a LoyaltyCost; mana abilities are recognised by the engine, CR 605. PayOnlyWith is the printed rider "activate only using mana produced by a creature" read as a colour restriction: the mana spent on this ability's cost must be of those colours (CR 106.6b, the spend restriction's other half). Leave it null for the ordinary case, where any mana pays. A restriction that names a source rather than a colour — "mana produced by artifacts" — is not this field; it goes to a primitive request, because paying with the wrong mana is a different game action, not a rounding error.

KeywordAbility.description: A keyword from CR 702 with its parameters: "Ward {2}" is Cost, "Bushido 2" is N, "Protection from red" and "Affinity for artifacts" are Of, "Partner with Name" is Detail. Cost is a printed mana string and takes nothing else. A keyword whose cost has a non-mana part — escape's "{1}{B}{B}, Exile four other cards from your graveyard" (CR 702.138a), and the "sacrifice a creature" half of several others — puts the whole cost in Costs as Cost records instead, mana included as a ManaCost entry, and leaves Cost null. Set one or the other, never both: two spellings of the same cost is how a card silently gets paid twice or not at all. Set Repeatable when the printed word says the cost may be paid more than once as the spell is cast: multikicker (CR 702.32b) and replicate-shaped keywords. Plain kicker (CR 702.32a) is paid once or not at all and leaves it false. A repeatable keyword is what makes the TimesKicked amount countable; without the flag, casting refuses a second payment, so a multikicker card translated without it is castable but never kicked twice.

SpellAbility.description: What an instant or sorcery does when it resolves, CR 113.3a.

StaticAbility.description: A continuous effect from a static ability, CR 604. Applies to objects via To or to players via Players.

TriggeredAbility.description: "When", "whenever", "at", CR 603. Where is the zone the ability functions in.

ChooseCost.description: "Pay {2} or sacrifice a creature": one of several costs, chosen when paying.

DiscardSelfCost.description: "Discard this card": the card the ability is on is the one discarded, and no other card can pay it. This is the cost cycling asks for — "[Cost], Discard this card: Draw a card" (CR 702.29a) — and the same shape jump-start and other discard-this-card abilities use. Use DiscardCost only when the text says "discard a card", where the player chooses which; a player must not be able to pay a discard-this-card cost with a different card.

ExileFromZoneCost.description: "Exile a creature card from your graveyard", "exile N cards from your hand".

LoyaltyCost.description: A loyalty ability's cost: +N, −N or 0, CR 606.

PayManaCost.description: Generic mana whose amount is counted from the game rather than printed, CR 118.8: "unless that player pays {X}, where X is this creature's power". Generic is the number of generic mana to pay, evaluated when the cost is announced (CR 601.2h); Colored is any printed coloured part paid alongside it ("{R} plus {X}"), written as printed. Use ManaCost for everything a card prints as a fixed symbol string, including "{X}" spelled with the spell's own X — this record is only for an amount the game has to count.

TapOther.description: "Tap an untapped creature you control": tap other permanents matching a filter.

TapUntappedCost.description: Convoke, improvise and "waterbend": tap untapped permanents in place of generic mana.

Adamant.description: Three or more mana of one color was spent to cast this spell.

AttackedThisTurn.description: "if you attacked with two or more creatures this turn": how many creatures a player declared as attackers this turn, compared against Min, CR 506.2 and 508.1. Counted over the whole turn and every combat phase in it, not just the current one, and a creature that was declared an attacker still counts after it has left combat or died. Raid is the same question with a minimum of one and is kept because the ability word is printed; use this record whenever the card names a number, and prefer it over Raid when the number is anything but one.

ChoiceIs.description: An earlier choice had a given value: "if the chosen color is red".

Compare.description: Any two amounts compared: "if your life total is less than an opponent's".

Controls.description: "if you control three or more artifacts": a count of objects compared to a number.

Corrupted.description: An opponent has three or more poison counters.

Coven.description: Three or more creatures with different powers.

Descend.description: Descend N: N or more permanent cards in your graveyard.

Ferocious.description: You control a creature with power 4 or greater.

FirstTimeThisTurn.description: "the first time this ability resolves each turn".

Formidable.description: Creatures you control have total power 8 or greater.

GiftPromised.description: "if the gift was promised", CR 702.174b: the caster of a spell with gift chose, as they cast it, to promise the gift to an opponent, and the spell's "if the gift was promised" clauses now apply. Promising is a choice made on casting, so this is answered from the spell's record of that choice, not from anything on the battlefield. Who names the player the gift was promised to when the card asks about them; leave it null for the plain "if the gift was promised" reading.

Matches.description: The selected object matches a filter: "if it's a creature card".

Paradox.description: You cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand this turn.

Raid.description: You attacked with a creature this turn.

Revolt.description: A permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn.

SpellMastery.description: Two or more instant and/or sorcery cards in your graveyard.

StoredIs.description: A stored count compared: "if two or more cards were discarded this way".

TargetsAre.description: The chosen targets satisfy a filter, checked at resolution.

CardRef.description: A card placed by a scenario. Alias is how steps and expectations refer to it when names repeat.

Effect.description: One instruction of a resolving spell or ability. The structural records combine instructions; the verbs in Effects.Verbs.cs and the keyword actions in Effects.Actions.cs do things. This is the whole list, and it is the name table.

Amount.description: A number a card refers to. Most are fixed; the rest are counted from the game when the effect resolves. Every derived record is registered here, and a test asserts that the list is complete.

ObjectFilter.description: A description of objects. Every field is optional and every set field must hold. This is the noun phrase of the game: "another nontoken creature you control with power 4 or greater" is one filter. Anything the fields cannot say goes in Also. Because the set fields are joined with "and", the fixed fields cannot say "or": "attacking or blocking creature" is not Attacking plus Blocking, which would match nothing. That one disjunction is common enough to have its own field — InCombat, true for a creature that is an attacking or a blocking creature (CR 506.2, 506.4) and false for one that is neither. Any other disjunction is written with AnyOf in Also.

ReplacedEvent.description: The event a replacement effect watches for, CR 614. The ability's With effect runs instead of the event, with Triggering bound to the object the event was about.

ContinuousEffect.description: What a continuous effect does to the objects or players it applies to, CR 611–613. Each record belongs to one layer, which the interpreter reads from the record type.

Selector.description: Which objects an instruction acts on. A selector names the objects; an ObjectFilter describes them. Targets are selectors, and so are "each creature", "this permanent" and "the exiled card".

PlayerRef.description: Which player or players an instruction means. "You" is the controller of the ability; everything else is relative to that or to the objects in play.

Trigger.description: The event a triggered ability watches for, CR 603. Each record names the event and describes the objects or players it must involve. The interpreter binds Triggering selectors to the matched objects.

Comparison.description: A comparison of some quantity against an amount: "power 4 or greater" is Ge 4.

AddMana.description: "Add {G}{G}", "add one mana of any color", "add X mana of the chosen color". Set SpendOnlyOn for a restricted mana: "add {C}. Spend this mana only to cast artifact spells" (CR 106.6a) — the filter describes what the mana may be spent on, and mana with a restriction is otherwise ordinary mana that empties from the pool as usual (CR 106.6b). Say "only to cast creature spells" as ObjectFilter(Spell: true, Types: CardType.Creature) and "only to activate abilities" with an ability filter; a restriction the filter cannot express goes to a primitive request rather than being dropped, because unrestricted mana is a different card.

Apply.description: "target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn", "gains flying until end of turn", "becomes a copy".

ApplyToPlayer.description: "You have no maximum hand size until end of turn": a continuous effect on a player.

Behold.description: "Behold a Dragon": reveal one from hand or choose one you control, remembered under a key.

ChangeTarget.description: "Change the target of target spell with a single target", CR 115.7: the spell or ability keeps resolving but points somewhere else. What selects the spell or ability on the stack; To names the new target when the card names it ("change its target to this creature") and is left null when the card lets a player choose. Set AllTargets for "you may choose new targets for it" (CR 114.6), which is the weaker action: it may leave the targets as they are, while a change must alter at least one (CR 115.7b). Legality is rechecked on resolution, so an illegal change is simply not made.

ChooseMode.description: "Choose one —", "choose two", "choose one or more". Entwine and escalate set Max to the mode count.

ChooseValue.description: "Choose a color", "choose a creature type", "choose a number": the choice is stored under a key.

CreateEmblem.description: A player gets an emblem (CR 114): an object in the command zone with no characteristics but the abilities the card gave it. Use this only when the card's own text prints those abilities, which is nearly always a planeswalker's ultimate ("You get an emblem with …"). An emblem the rules define rather than the card — the Ring, CR 701.54b — is RingTemptsYou, and the engine supplies its abilities; see that record's remarks.

DealDamage.description: "Deals 3 damage": to objects through To, to players through ToPlayer, or to both when the card names both ("deals 2 damage to target creature and 2 damage to that creature's controller"). The three words "any target" are not both halves written out: they are the AnyTarget selector in To, with ToPlayer left out (CR 115.4). Use the two halves together only when the card really names two things to damage.

DealDividedDamage.description: "deals 4 damage divided as you choose among one, two, three, or four targets".

DelayedTrigger.description: "At the beginning of the next end step, return it." A trigger created by this effect, CR 603.7.

DistributeCounters.description: "Distribute three +1/+1 counters among one, two, or three target creatures", CR 601.2d: the division is announced as the spell is cast, every named target gets at least one counter, and no more than MaxTargets targets may be chosen. N is the total distributed, Counter the kind, and Among the target selector, whose own Count is the number of targets and is normally left null so MaxTargets rules it. This is the counter twin of DealDividedDamage; do not spell a division as ForEach over targets, which would give every target the whole amount.

EntersAs.description: Inside a replacement: the entering object enters as a copy, transformed, face down, or under another's control.

EntersTapped.description: Inside a replacement: the entering object enters tapped.

EntersWithCounters.description: Inside a replacement: the entering object enters with counters.

Flip.description: "Flip it", CR 710.2: a flip permanent is turned upside down and its alternative (FaceRole.Flipped) face's name, types, abilities and power/toughness apply. This is not transform (CR 701.27a), which turns a double-faced card over to its back face, and not FlipCoin, which is CR 705. A flip is one way only — CR 710.4 has no action that unflips — so a card that "returns it to its unflipped state" is a different mechanic and goes to a primitive request. Use this record whenever the printed text says the permanent flips, whatever the layout says.

ForEach.description: "For each creature you control, ...". Inside, Triggering is the current object.

ForEachPlayer.description: "Each player ...", in APNAP order. Inside, TriggeringPlayer is the current player.

If.description: "If you do, ...", "if it's a creature card, ...".

LookAt.description: "Look at target player's hand", "look at the top four cards of your library".

May.description: "You may ...": the player decides on resolution. Who defaults to you.

MayCast.description: "You may cast it without paying its mana cost", "you may cast that card this turn".

MayPlay.description: "You may play that card this turn" (lands included).

ModifyAmount.description: Inside a replacement: the event happens with its number changed: "draw twice that many", "gain that much life plus 1".

Move.description: The one zone-change verb: "return target creature to its owner's hand", "put it onto the battlefield tapped", "put that card on the bottom of your library". Exile and sacrifice have their own records because the rules name them.

PayCost.description: "You may pay {4}. If you do, ..." — a cost paid inside a resolving effect, CR 118.12. The cost is paid where it stands rather than as part of casting or activating, so it composes: wrap it in May with a StoreChoiceAs key for "you may pay", and follow it with If(ChoiceIs(key, "yes"), ...) for the "if you do" half. Use Unless for "unless that player pays", where the cost belongs to someone else and the effect is what happens when it goes unpaid. Any Cost record works here, including PayManaCost for an amount counted from the game.

Prepare.description: Prepare, CR 702.180: the object gains the Prepared designation, which lasts until something takes it away and is not a counter and not an ability. Ask about it with the IsPrepared predicate.

PreventThatDamage.description: Inside a damage replacement: prevent that damage, all of it or an amount.

PutPlayerCounters.description: Poison, energy, experience, rad and ticket counters on a player; negative amounts remove.

Remember.description: Remember the objects a selector resolves to under a key, for later steps.

Reorder.description: "Put them back in any order", "in a random order".

ReplaceWith.description: Inside a replacement: the whole event is replaced by this effect; "instead".

RevealUntil.description: Cascade-shaped: reveal from the top until a match; remember the match and the rest separately.

RingTemptsYou.description: The Ring tempts you (CR 701.54): you get the emblem named The Ring if you do not have it, and then choose a creature you control as your Ring-bearer.

Sacrifice.description: "Sacrifice a creature": the player chooses; "sacrifice it": a selector.

Search.description: "Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle." One zone goes in From. A card that searches several at once — "search your graveyard, hand, and library for a card named ..." — puts every zone in Zones in printed order and leaves From alone; the whole search is one action over the union, so a single card is found across all of them (CR 701.23a). Shuffling follows CR 701.23c: a library that was searched is shuffled afterwards and other zones are not, so a multi-zone search with ShuffleAfter set shuffles only the libraries among Zones. Set ShuffleOnlyIfFound for the printed rider "if you do, shuffle" / "shuffle only if you searched your library this way", where no shuffle happens when the search found nothing there.

Sequence.description: Instructions in order. "Draw two cards, then discard a card."

Store.description: A choice a player is asked to make, or a value an effect records for later steps.

Unless.description: "Counter target spell unless its controller pays {3}."

Unprepare.description: Unprepare, CR 702.180: the object loses the Prepared designation. Nothing happens if it was not prepared.

Unsupported.description: The translator could not express something in this vocabulary. A file containing this fails the linter and never reaches a game; the pipeline ranks these to find the next primitive.

Vote.description: Voting: each player votes for one option; the effect of the winning option runs, or per-vote effects.

CardsInZoneOf.description: "the number of creature cards in your graveyard": cards in a zone, optionally filtered.

ChosenNumber.description: A number chosen earlier in the same effect with Choose.

CountOf.description: "the number of creatures you control": objects matching a filter.

CountersOn.description: Counters of one kind on an object; any kind when Counter is null.

CountersOnPlayer.description: Poison, energy, experience and other counters a player has.

Devotion.description: Devotion to one or more colors, CR 700.5: the number of mana symbols of those colors among the mana costs of permanents that player controls. Normally the colors are printed and go in Colors ("your devotion to black"). When the card instead reads "your devotion to the chosen color", leave Colors at Colorless and set ChosenColorKey to the key an earlier ChooseValue(ChooseWhat.Color, key) step stored the colour under; the colour is then read from that choice when the amount is counted. Never emit a fixed colour for a chosen one — the two are different cards.

Domain.description: The number of basic land types among lands a player controls.

GreatestAmong.description: "the greatest power among creatures you control".

ManaSpentOnThis.description: Mana spent to cast this spell, CR 601.2h.

Stored.description: A number an earlier step produced: "the number of cards discarded this way".

TimesKicked.description: How many times this spell was kicked, CR 702.32b: multikicker's cost may be paid any number of times as the spell is cast, and "for each time it was kicked" counts those payments. Use this for multikicker and for replicate-shaped repeated optional costs; a card with plain kicker (CR 702.32a, paid once or not at all) asks WasKickedCondition instead, which is a yes or no. The KeywordAbility this counts must carry Repeatable, or nothing ever pays it twice.

TotalAmong.description: "the total power of creatures you control".

X.description: The X paid or chosen for the spell or ability, CR 107.3.

Predicate.description: The long tail of object descriptions the fixed fields of ObjectFilter cannot express.

WouldBePutIntoZone.description: "If a card would be put into your graveyard from anywhere".

WouldBeginStep.description: "Skip your draw step", "if a player would begin their turn".

WouldDie.description: "If this creature would die, exile it instead."

WouldEnterBattlefield.description: "As this creature enters", "if a creature would enter under your control".

AddTypes.description: Adds card types, subtypes or supertypes in layer 4 (CR 613.1d) while keeping the ones already there: "is a creature in addition to its other types", "is also a Goblin". Set AllCreatureTypes when the object is every creature type at once — changeling (CR 702.72a) and any text reading "is every creature type" (CR 205.3d). Say it with that flag, never by listing creature types: the list changes with every set, and the engine derives it rather than carrying card data.

BecomesCopyOf.description: Layer 1: becomes a copy of another object, with the printed exceptions.

CantBeBlocked.description: "can't be blocked", "can't be blocked by creatures with power 2 or less", "can't be blocked except by two or more creatures".

CantBeTargeted.description: Shroud and hexproof are keywords; this is the general form: "can't be the target of red spells".

CostModifier.description: "Instant and sorcery spells you cast cost {1} less": positive delta is an increase.

ManaProducesAdditional.description: "Whenever you tap a Forest for mana, add an additional {G}."

MayPlayFromZone.description: "You may play lands from your graveyard", "you may cast spells from the top of your library". With WithoutPayingManaCost, "you may cast it this turn without paying its mana cost" (CR 118.9): the permission also waives the mana cost of the cast it allows.

MustBeBlocked.description: "All creatures able to block it do so."

PlayerCant.description: A prohibition that applies to a player rather than to an object: "your life total can't change", "you can't lose the game", "you can't be the target of spells", "prevent all damage that would be dealt to you". Apply it with a StaticAbility whose Players is set, or with ApplyToPlayer for a duration; the Selector-shaped To is not used for these. Several restrictions can be set at once because PlayerRestriction is a flag set. CantLoseGame, CantWinGame and CantGainLife stay as they are — they were already spelled that way in card files and mean exactly what they say; use this record for the restrictions they do not cover.

PlayerProtectionFromEverything.description: "You have protection from everything", CR 702.16j: the player can't be targeted by spells or abilities their opponents control, all damage that would be dealt to them is prevented, and they can't be enchanted. Protection on an object is the KeywordAbility Protection with its Of filter; this is the player-scoped form, which the keyword cannot carry because a player is not an object. Apply it through a StaticAbility with Players set, or ApplyToPlayer for a duration.

PreventDamage.description: Prevention, CR 615: all when Amount is null.

AnyTarget.description: "Any target", CR 115.4: exactly one target chosen from among every creature, player, planeswalker and battle. This is the whole phrase in one selector, and it is the only spelling of it. Do not write it as a Target whose filter names Creature, Planeswalker and Battle beside a toPlayer, and do not write it as an open filter beside a toPlayer: the first cannot say the player half and the second lets the damage hit a land. On DealDamage it goes in To, and ToPlayer is then left out — To of AnyTarget already means "whichever of the four was chosen". The chosen target is announced as the spell or ability is put on the stack (CR 601.2c): an object target rides in the command's Targets and a player target in its TargetPlayers, so the two halves are one choice at cast time and the resolving effect deals its damage to whichever half the stack entry holds. Count, UpTo and Key are here for the same reason Target carries them: "any number of target creatures" has its counterpart in "up to one target", divided damage names several targets (CR 601.2d), and a later step refers back by Key. Count absent means one.

Attached.description: The object this Aura, Equipment or Fortification is attached to: "enchanted creature", "equipped creature".

Attachments.description: Objects attached to this one, optionally filtered.

Choose.description: A non-targeted choice: "choose a creature you control". The chooser picks when the effect resolves.

Each.description: "each creature", "all artifacts": every object matching the filter, no targeting.

RandomFrom.description: "a card at random from your hand".

Remembered.description: Objects an earlier step produced and remembered under a key: "the exiled card", "those tokens".

Self.description: This object: the permanent with the ability, or the spell being cast.

SourceOfDamage.description: The source of the damage a trigger or replacement is about.

Target.description: "target creature", "up to two target players' creatures". Key lets later steps refer back.

ThisSpellsTargets.description: The targets this spell or ability chose, for effects that refer back to them collectively.

Top.description: "the top card of your library", "the top three cards of target player's library".

Triggering.description: The object the trigger was about, or the other object involved: "that creature", "it", "the blocked creature".

ChoosePlayer.description: A non-targeted player choice: "choose a player".

DefendingPlayer.description: The player being attacked, or the controller of the planeswalker or battle being attacked.

PlayerWithMostOf.description: "the player with the most life", "the player who controls the most creatures".

TargetPlayer.description: "target player" or "target opponent". Names a key so later steps can refer back.

TriggeringPlayer.description: The player the trigger was about: the one who drew, discarded, was dealt damage.

You.description: The controller of the spell or ability.

AnyOfTriggers.description: "Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery": several events, one ability.

AtStep.description: "At the beginning of your upkeep", "at the beginning of each end step".

Attacks.description: "Whenever this creature attacks", "whenever a creature you control attacks a planeswalker".

BecomesTarget.description: "Whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability".

ChapterReached.description: A Saga chapter, CR 714. Chapter abilities are triggered abilities with this trigger.

CounterPlaced.description: "Whenever one or more +1/+1 counters are put on a creature you control"; Nth for "the third".

DealsDamage.description: "Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player", "whenever a source you control deals damage".

Dies.description: "Whenever a creature dies": put into a graveyard from the battlefield, CR 700.4.

EntersBattlefield.description: "When this creature enters", "Whenever another creature you control enters".

LandPlayed.description: Landfall: "whenever a land enters under your control" is EntersBattlefield; this is the play itself.

RoomUnlocked.description: A Room's door is unlocked, CR 709.5: the half gains its unlocked designation.

ZoneChange.description: Any other zone change: "whenever a card is put into your graveyard from anywhere".

ManaProduction.description: What a mana instruction produces. Fixed is printed mana ("{G}{G}"); otherwise one of the described choices.

Duration.description: How long an effect lasts, CR 611. A static ability's effect lasts while its source is on the battlefield and needs no duration; everything created by a resolving effect names one.

EmblemSpec.description: The emblem an effect creates, CR 114.1: a name for the log and the abilities it has.

TokenSpec.description: A token to create, CR 111. The pipeline fills it from Scryfall's all_parts and the token's own card object; ScryfallOracleId keeps the link.

AttachedTo.description: Attached to the given object: "Auras attached to it".

CanBlock.description: Able to block the given attacker right now.

CouldBlock.description: Could block the given creature if it were attacking, ignoring whether combat is happening.

HasAbilityOfKind.description: Has an ability of the given kind: "a creature with a mana ability", "with an activated ability".

IsAttached.description: Attached to anything at all, or unattached when false.

IsPrepared.description: Carries the Prepared designation, CR 702.180: "prepared creatures you control", "if it's prepared". The designation is put on by the Prepare effect and taken off by Unprepare; it is not a counter, so WithCounter does not see it.

IsThisObject.description: The object this ability is printed on, and nothing else. "This" in a card's text always means the object the ability is on (CR 109.5), so a trigger that is about its own source says it with this predicate: "whenever this creature attacks" is Attacks with ObjectFilter(Also: IsThisObject), and "whenever this creature dies" is Dies with the same filter (CR 603.2 — a trigger's event is matched against its own source like any other object). Do not confuse it with Other, which means "another" and excludes this object, or with an unmarked filter, which matches every object it describes including this one. The selector Self is the same idea on the effect side: use Self to act on this object, IsThisObject to describe it inside a filter.

ProducesMana.description: A source that could produce mana of the given colors.

SharesTypeWith.description: Shares a card type — or, with CreatureTypeOnly, a creature type — with the object With names. This is how a relation between two objects the same effect touched is written, and it is the answer to the shape translators reach for a new record for: "search your library for two basic land cards that share a land type" is a Sequence whose first step searches and remembers the first card, and whose second step searches for one that shares a type with it — Sequence([Search(basicLand, Battlefield, RememberAs: "first"), Search(new ObjectFilter(Types: CardType.Land, Supertypes: Supertype.Basic, Also: new SharesTypeWith(new Remembered("first"), CreatureTypeOnly: false)), Zone.Battlefield)]). Remember plus this predicate expresses every "that share a ..." and "with the same ..." relation; SharesColorWith and SharesNameWith are the same pattern for colour and name.

TargetedBy.description: Currently targeted by the given object, typically Self.

PlayerFilter.description: Who qualifies for a player choice or target.

ForAsLongAs.description: "for as long as you control an artifact".

UntilLeaves.description: "for as long as that creature remains on the battlefield".

UntilStep.description: "until the beginning of your next upkeep", "until the end of your next turn".
